durationPrevalidation.reason: Extra Rust boundary showed no consistent benefit; DateTime addition slowed in both Rust variants. Existing early JS validation preserves options order; public Rust Duration/core operations still validate independently.

control.method: Fresh sequential native-data WASM processes, Rust/JS/JS/Rust prevalidation order. Same four matched arithmetic workloads, eight varying inputs/parity, 20000 warmup and nine samples of 50000 calls. Rust binary identical between variants; only duration prevalidation delegation differs.

rawLocalResolution.reason: Alternating controls consistently improve parse/round/day start relative to field round trips. Both variants retain bounds-only DateTime checks and bounded offset-hint visitation. DateTime parse controls vary and do not establish a per-variant gain.

control.method: Fresh sequential native-data WASM processes, nanoseconds/fields/fields/nanoseconds. Same four public workloads, eight inputs/parity, 20000 warmup and nine samples of 50000 calls. Both variants retain bounds-only DateTime constructor validation and bounded offset-hint visitation. Only the larger raw local-resolution/day-boundary refactor differs.

trustedZonedConstruction.reason: Modest alternating-control parse/add/round gains; day-start changes mixed. Same prototype/brands and numeric user-input validation. Not a universal stable-win claim.

control.method: Fresh sequential native-data WASM processes, checked/trusted/trusted/checked construction. Same four public zoned workloads, eight inputs/parity, 20000 warmup and nine samples of 50000 calls. Rust binary unchanged; trusted construction accepts only private branded or Rust-result slots, with numeric user constructors unchanged.
